text:
Nice way to end the weekend. We're still in the low 60s as the sun heads down around 5:52, and the sky is clear, so the sunset should be a good one. Grab a jacket if you're heading out for it, because it cools off quickly once the sun's gone. Clouds drift in overnight and we settle to around 41, so tonight is chilly but not frosty in town.

Monday starts with some sun, then clouds build ahead of a dry cold front. I wouldn't count on rain. A sprinkle is possible, but Burlington should stay dry, and the front clears out by early afternoon. The high is near 57, and the wind turns north behind the front.

That's the start of a real change. Monday night drops to the mid 30s, and Tuesday is sunny but struggles to reach the upper 40s. Plan on a warm coat for Tuesday, and scrape the windshield Wednesday morning.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-25T18:20:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. A weak, moisture starved, cold front will pass through the area tomorrow, with sharply colder temperatures heading towards mid week.
  2. Moderating temperatures are expected late this week and next weekend with some brief rain possible Thursday night.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 219 PM EDT Sunday... No significant changes to the current forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure today will begin to depart tonight into tomorrow evening with the approach of a weak, moisture starved cold front for tomorrow. GOES-19 visible satellite shows this front nicely with a narrow band of cloud cover stretched across the Michigan Upper Peninsula to west central Quebec. As the front moves into northern New York tomorrow morning, antecedent dry conditions at the surface will limit much if not all of the precipitation that will be associated with the boundary. Virga looks likely with dewpoint depressions of 5-10 degrees ahead of the front. A few places along the northwest facing slopes of the Adirondacks and northern Greens, including Jay Peak, may see a few sprinkles, but accumulations will be little to non-measureable. In the deeper valleys, we will likely not have enough time to saturate before dry air advects in behind the boundary cutting off any precipitation chances by tomorrow early afternoon. Winds will turn to the north- northwest as the front moves through advecting sharply colder air from Canada. Monday night lows will cool to the upper 20s for many locations with a few locations hovering around the freezing mark in the wider valleys. Tuesday will feature sunny skies with continued cool high temperatures struggling to reach the upper 40s. The coldest night of the season arrives Tuesday night under strong radiational cooling. Overnight lows may approach some records for Montpelier and St. Johnsbury, with records elsewhere residing in the 10th percentile or lower. Temperatures will drop to the teens across the Adirondacks and low 20s elsewhere. Temperatures slowly rebound Wednesday as high pressure and south winds help to moderate our flow pattern. KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure overhead will allow the air mass to slowly moderate Wednesday night into next weekend with highs climbing back into the upper 50s and 60s on Thursday and Friday. There is the potential for a few showers on Thursday night with another weak cold front, about 30-60% chance of rain outside of central and south- central Vermont, which have lower chances, closer to 10-40%. The forecast for Halloween trick-or-treating looks dry and seasonably mild under high pressure with afternoon temperatures in the upper 50s to mid 60s, falling into the lower and mid 50s in the evening.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Today will continue the dry and sunny weather, except it will be pleasantly warmer with highs in the upper 50s to mid-60s. It will be excellent for checking out the remaining fall foliage. Though we’re past peak at this point, there are still some trees that have nice color. Tonight won’t be as cold due to a gentle southwest breeze ahead of a cold front. That front will pass through mainly dry on Monday, but a few sprinkles are possible in northern parts of the region. Highs will be in the 50s. Much cooler air will move in behind this front. Tuesday will be a nice-looking day, but it will be quite chilly with highs only in the 40s. You’ll certainly want a jacket. Lows will be in the 20s, though some teens are likely. Wednesday will be a bit warmer with sunny skies and highs in the upper 40s to low 50s. Thursday will be pleasant with some low 60s expected. Another front will move through Thursday night. Some showers are possible along that, but no significant rain is expected. Any showers will end Friday morning, with the rest of the day being partly sunny and fair. Halloween looks good for trick-or-treaters with mostly sunny skies and highs mainly in the mid-50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-25T13:26:00Z — same caveat): Sunny and warmer Sunday, after another frosty start — High pressure stays nearby Sunday, bringing full sunshine! It turns warmer, thanks to a light south breeze that develops. Highs reach the mid-60s. Clouds increase tonight, and it will be seasonably cold with patchy frost. Lows will be near 40 in the Champlain Valley, but most towns fall to the upper 20s and 30s. After some early rays of sun, Monday turns mostly cloudy with a few spot showers in northern areas, due to a cold front on approach. Highs reach the upper 50s there. Southern Vermont looks brighter overall, where highs again push well into the 60s. Behind that front, a shot of unseasonable cold arrives Tuesday, as highs fall back to the mid-40s. Expect a mostly sunny sky, with a noticeable north breeze. Wednesday starts with another widespread freeze, but it turns seasonable by afternoon, with highs in the low 50s and a mostly sunny sky. Another warmup arrives late week with highs near 60, thanks to a gusty south breeze. A few showers are likely Thursday night into Friday, with another cold front on approach, though not anticipating any significant rain. Halloween weekend looks dry and seasonable, with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs reach the low 60s.
